newsitem.title: MEXICO: Latam stocks seen buoyant on follow-through.
newsitem.headline: Latam stocks seen buoyant on follow-through.

text.p: Investors can look forward to Latin American shares cautiously continuing their recent upward march this week on capital flows to the region, stock market specialists said.
Analysts in Mexico said a pause was likely after last week's string of record gains on the bourse had far outstripped all previous expectations, but the overall upward trend was clearly marked.
"Of course, it certainly can go up on the basis of the (capital) flows we have seen," said Felix Boni, research chief at ING-Barings in Mexico.
"But I am always concerned when you have too much of a good thing at any one time," he added.
Stockwatchers pointed out the bulls were still charging even though stocks were very overbought from a technical standpoint and long overdue for profit-taking.
"It's a bull market. Investors, particularly from North America are puring money into the region," said Geoffrey Dennis, an investment strategist at HSBC-James Capel in New York.
The leading IPC share index of Mexican stocks closed at 4,439.14 points on Friday, up 194.51 points or 4.58 percent on the week, which saw five straight record closes.
Brazilian stocks should also maintain their upside trend this week as local fixed-income funds continue to pour money into equities and investors adjust portfolios ahead of month's end, brokers said.

But volume should be thinner and rises will be moderate as only light congressional activity is foreseen. Many lawmakers from Brazil's north and northeast are expected to take off part of the week in observance of Tuesday's St. John's Day holiday.
The bolsa's Bovespa index of 48 most-traded shares rose 2.4 percent last week on hefty volume, closing Friday at 12,121 points. So far this month, the Sao Paulo bourse is up 6.6 percent.
Argentine stocks were expected to push cautiously higher, following through on the momentum of the past several weeks which traders attributed to stronger foreign cash flows.
"The outlook remains good, especially because the market made a healthy pause Friday and will soon be ready to aim for new highs," said Gabriel Ruiz at brokers Tavelli.
The blue-chip MerVal index shed 0.4 percent Friday to 822.5, trimming gains in the week to 1.1 percent.
It had closed at a five-year high of 826.12 Thursday, when volume surged to a hefty 52 million pesos -- the strongest tally seen in more than three years.

Despite an expected slowdown due to the Battle of Carabobo market holiday Tuesday, Venezuelan stocks are seen maintaining the head of steam they built up last week on ground-breaking labor reforms, traders said.
"The trend definitely remains up," Cavelba broker Harold Cuellar said.
Stocks closed up Friday 6.3 percent on the week at 8008.93 points as investors cheered the signing into law of an historic $14 billion Labor Law reform bill.
After falling for most of last week, Chilean stocks are seen finding their footing this week although the market will still be vulnerable to a renewed bout of profit-taking, said traders.
International investors, who poured into the market after a recent rate cut, are likely to remain on the sidelines with most trade next week from Chilean buyers, said traders.
"Some local buyers could return to the market on speculation sone companies could report strong first half earnings," said Valentin Carril of Santander Investments.
Firms are due to report their earnings at the end of July although results often filter into the bourse weeks before.
The blue chip index ended the week down 2.4 percent at 132.9 points.
